Lauer concludes by noting the high number of 'loose votes' in the electorate and the scarcity of fresh polls expected in April.

Title: Sondeo muestra a dos candidatos de derecha liderando la carrera por llegar al balotaje en Perú

Summary: 
According to a survey conducted by Datum Internacional between February 27 and March 4 and released on March 9, 2026, right-wing candidates Keiko Fujimori and Rafael López Aliaga are tied for the lead in Peru's upcoming presidential election, which is expected to go to a runoff. The survey also found that 38.5% of voters remain undecided or plan not to vote, reflecting political disinterest in a country that has had eight presidents since 2018 due to resignations or corruption scandals. Other candidates include Alfonso López-Chau (5.5%), César Acuña (5.2%), Carlos Álvarez (5.0%), and Wolfgang Crozo (4.2%). Urpi Torrado, CEO of Datum Internacional, noted that leading in polls does not guarantee victory, as many Peruvians decide their vote close to election day. With 36 candidates—a record for the country—a first-round winner is not expected, and the electoral authority has scheduled a runoff for June 7, 2026.

Title: Un debate inédito de seis días reunirá a 36 candidatos por la presidencia de Perú

Summary: 
The National Electoral Jury (JNE) announced an unprecedented six-day televised debate featuring all 36 presidential candidates in Peru, the largest field in the country's recent electoral history. The candidates will be divided into groups of twelve per day, with four groups of three candidates each, over six dates from March 23 to April 1. Topics include citizen security, crime prevention, corruption, education, and employment. The debate format is a response to the extreme political fragmentation in Peru. Among the candidates are a former national football player, a television comedian, and an individual who is a fugitive from justice on corruption charges. Rafael López Aliaga, a right-wing former mayor of Lima, leads the polls with 13.4% of voting intention, followed by Keiko Fujimori, daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, with 9.7%, according to a recent Datum survey. The winner will succeed interim president José María Balcázar, a leftist who assumed power the previous week amid a deep political crisis. Since 2016, Peru has had eight different leaders—four removed by Congress, two who resigned, and only one who completed their interim term. Over 27.3 million Peruvians are eligible to vote on April 12 to elect a president, 130 congressmen, and 60 senators. If no candidate receives over 50% of the vote, a runoff election will be held in June between the top two candidates.

Published date: February 25 2026, 02:24

Peru is heading toward a chaotic presidential election on April 12, 2026, with 36 candidates vying for the presidency, following a political crisis that led to the removal of interim President José Jerí and his replacement by Congressman José María Balcázar. Balcázar’s interim presidency is expected to last only 150 days, but political instability means his tenure could be cut short at any time.

Title: Los peruanos afrontan desconcertados una elección presidencial con 36 candidatos

Summary: 
Peruvians face the presidential election on April 12, 2026, with bewilderment due to a record 36 candidates, including a fugitive from justice, a TV comedian, and ex-military figures, according to reports from AFP. Sociologist David Sulmont attributes the difficulty in finding a convincing candidate to the fragmentation of the political landscape, which has broken the power balance between the Parliament and the Executive. Additionally, an RPP radio report states that at least 252 candidates for all positions hold criminal convictions, complicating the process for citizens. Despite this political instability and a general perception of corruption and inefficiency, Peru remains one of Latin America's most stable economies, registering the region's lowest inflation rate of 1.5% in 2025.

Title: Perú: una proliferación de candidatos presidenciales que revela un malestar político

Summary: 
Peru is experiencing a record number of 34 presidential candidates for the April 2026 elections, the highest in the country's history, reflecting deep political instability and fragmentation. This surge comes amid a crisis marked by seven presidents in the past nine years and widespread distrust in the political class, which new political movements are seeking to exploit. The candidates span from the center-left to the far-right, with no major figure generating strong public enthusiasm—48% of voters remain undecided. In the latest polls, far-right former Lima mayor Rafael López Aliaga leads with 10%, followed by Keiko Fujimori at 7%, and Mario Vizcarra (brother of former president Martín Vizcarra, convicted of corruption and barred from running) at 5%. Actor-comedian Carlos Álvarez, who styles himself as the 'Peruvian Bukele,' ranks fourth with 4%, and social democrat Alfonso López Chao comes fifth with 3%. The extreme fragmentation of the vote raises the possibility of a runoff between two candidates with low support. The same election will also determine members of the Senate, Congress, and the Andean Parliament.

Title: Candidato à Presidência do Peru morre em acidente de trânsito

Summary: 
Napoleón Becerra, a 61-year-old presidential candidate for the Party of Workers and Entrepreneurs (PTE) in Peru, died in a car accident on Sunday, March 15, while traveling to a campaign event. Balvin Huamani, the mayor of the Pilpichaca district, confirmed to the RPP broadcaster that he personally transported Becerra to a health post where his death was verified. The National Electoral Court (JNE) expressed condolences and wished a speedy recovery to the three injured passengers accompanying Becerra. Only Francisco Sagasti completed his interim term (2020–July 2021). Pedro Castillo was removed and arrested in December 2022, and his successor, José Jeri, was impeached in February 2026 for 'misconduct' and alleged influence peddling involving Chinese businessmen. José María Balcázar, from the left-wing Peru Libre party, is serving as the current interim president until July 2026. If no candidate secures over 50% of the vote, a runoff will take place in June between the top two contenders, with the winner set to assume office on July 28.
